figures.caption: Figure 3. Dataset characteristics and performance evaluation of PathPocket on text-only pathology benchmarks. A. Distribution of anatomical systems involved in the public medical licensing examination datasets, including USMLE (n=133) and NMLE (n=142). B. Distribution of pathology question types (e.g., diagnosis, treatment, etiology & risk) within the public USMLE and NMLE datasets. C. Demographic and clinical characteristics of the large-scale private clinical dataset, SMU-Text (n=1,854). The donut charts illustrate the distribution of patient age, gender, benign/malignant tumor status, and anatomical systems, reflecting a highly diverse and representative real-world clinical cohort. D. Accuracy comparison between PathPocket and baseline large language models (Qwen3 series ranging from 0.5B to 30B parameters) across six public examination datasets (USMLE 1-3 and NMLE 2022-2024). PathPocket achieves performance comparable to or exceeding the 30B parameter model. E. Accuracy comparison on six independent sub-tasks of the private real-world SMU-Text dataset (SMU-Text 1 to 6). PathPocket consistently outperforms all baseline models, demonstrating the superiority of its evidence grounded reasoning in complex, real-world clinical scenarios. Error bars represent the 95% confidence intervals, and p-values indicate statistical significance between PathPocket and the best-performing baseline.

Figure 4. Performance of PathPocket on ROI-level multimodal clinical pathology benchmarks. A. Accuracy comparison on three public region-of-interest (ROI) datasets (BreakHis, CCRCC, and Chaoyang). PathPocket significantly outperforms both general vision-language models (Qwen3VL series) and medical-specific vision-language models (LLaVA-Med, Quilt-LLaVA) (p < 0.05). B–D. Characteristics and evaluation of the private SMU-281 dataset, which contains complex clinical questions meticulously crafted by 15 expert pathologists. B. Distribution of anatomical systems. C. Number of ROI images provided per case. D. Accuracy comparison across four anatomical sub-tasks (Breast, GI & HPB, Head & Neck & Thyroid, and Other) and the overall average. PathPocket demonstrates superior multimodal reasoning compared to baselines. E–G. Characteristics and evaluation of the large-scale private SMU-VL dataset (n = 4,937), with multimodal tasks directly derived from real-world pathology reports. E. Distribution of images per case (note the log scale on the x-axis, with the majority containing 4 images). F. Demographic and clinical distributions of the SMU-VL cohort, including age, gender, benign/malignant status, and anatomical systems. G. Accuracy comparison across six independent sub-tasks (SMU-VL 1 to 6). PathPocket consistently maintains robust performance, outperforming the best baseline models. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

Figure 6. Qualitative comparison of diagnostic reasoning between standard LLM/MLLM baselines and the evidence grounded PathPocket. A. Text-only clinical case (Cardiac Mass): The baseline Qwen3 model misinterprets the complex immunohistochemistry (IHC) profile, incorrectly asserting that S-100 negativity excludes atrial myxoma and hallucinating the IHC criteria for rhabdomyosarcoma. In contrast, PathPocket correctly diagnoses Atrial Myxoma (B), explicitly refutes the rhabdomyosarcoma differential by citing the lack of required markers (MyoD1, Myogenin), and grounds its explanation in specific retrieved textbooks and atlases. B. Multimodal clinical case (Renal Mass): Given clinical history and microscopic ROI images, the baseline Qwen3VL misinterprets the morphology as a benign adenoma. PathPocket accurately correlates the visual features (papillary structures, clear/lightly stained cells) with the clinical presentation (exophytic nodule, mildly increased metabolism) to correctly identify a Clear Cell Papillary Renal Cell Tumor (C). Crucially, PathPocket supports its multimodal differential diagnosis by citing authoritative clinical guidelines (e.g., CSCO, CACA) and standard renal pathology textbooks.

Figure 5. Performance of PathPocket on gigapixel Whole-Slide Image (WSI) multimodal clinical tasks. A–C. Characteristics of the private WSI-level clinical dataset (n = 1,232). A. Distribution of anatomical systems, comprising Gastric (56.8%), Colorectal (36.0%), and Breast (7.1%) tissues. B. Distribution of complex diagnostic tasks, including tumor Grading (39.6%), Staging (36.0%), and Subtyping (24.4%). C. Study design distribution, highlighting the inclusion of both retrospective (87.8%) and highly challenging prospective (12.2%) clinical cases. D. Accuracy comparison between PathPocket and the Qwen3VL baseline models (2B, 4B, and 8B) across the overall dataset and five specific WSI-level tasks: Retrospective Gastric Cancer Grading, Retrospective Gastric Subtyping, Prospective Gastric Cancer Subtyping, Retrospective Colorectal Cancer (CRC) T-Staging, and Retrospective Breast Cancer Grading. PathPocket demonstrates a substantial and statistically significant advantage over general vision-language models in processing and reasoning over gigapixel WSIs (e.g., Overall p < 0.05). Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals, and p-values denote the significance level compared to the best-performing baseline.

Figure 2. Construction and characterization of the large-scale multimodal pathology evidence hypergraph. A. Distribution of the curated 110,472 source documents across various anatomical systems, demonstrating comprehensive coverage of human pathology. B–C. Distribution of medical evidence levels (graded according to an 8-tier hierarchy) at the document level (B) and the parsed semantic chunk level (C). While Case Reports (Level 5) constitute the majority of individual documents (64.4%), dense sources such as Textbooks (Level 7) and Guidelines (Level 1) yield a disproportionately large share of the 1,557,055 semantic knowledge chunks (21.3% and 4.0%, respectively). D. Distribution of extracted entity types within the hypergraph. Crucially, multimodal elements such as “Image” (n > 350,000) and “Table” are integrated with clinical entities within the hypergraph. E. Distribution of the relation types connecting the entities. The network is heavily populated with clinically actionable relationships, forming a densely connected knowledge topology. F. Hyperedges by entity count. Distribution of the total 7,100,480 hyperedges categorized by the number of connected entities per hyperedge. The x-axis is shown on a log scale.
